BERT4Rec requires masked-target training and appended-mask inference. RecTools explicitly implements left padding, truncation to reserve one mask position, and prediction from the appended token. For this task, read the final nonpadding position; `count_nonzero-1` is incorrect for left-padded sequences. These provide concrete deployment assertions rather than assuming arbitrary padding changes preserve scores—absolute position embeddings can invalidate that assumption. [RecTools implementation](https://rectools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/rectools/models/nn/transformers/bert4rec.html)

A proposed bounded verification suite: replay fixed public histories through the in-memory category model and actual exported `working/predict.py`, comparing canonical input IDs, appended-mask location, candidate-aligned scores within calibrated numerical tolerance, and rankings with explicit tie handling. Exercise short, near-limit and truncated histories across all four routes. Harmless controls include batch reordering, singleton versus batched inference, repeated calls, and candidate permutations reversed before comparison. Persist and verify category, architecture configuration, item-map digest, special-token IDs and checkpoint digest; strict weight loading alone cannot detect a same-shaped wrong checkpoint or mapping. PyTorch requires evaluation mode for inference; TensorFlow recommends shared preprocessing to prevent training-serving skew. [PyTorch](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html), [TensorFlow](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfx/guide/tft_bestpractices)

Calibrate with deliberately injected, verified faults: count-based readout, omitted mask, swapped item IDs, wrong category routing and mismatched configuration/checkpoint. Report detected faults and false alarms on harmless controls, without retraining or claiming measured detection beforehand. This is a task-specific proposal supported by 2025 model-level metamorphic-testing research, not an established BERT4Rec deployment benchmark. Each comparison uses the same single trained category model; no score fusion or additional fitted predictors. [2025 study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04354)
